Sure. Once the redesigned room image is ready, we call our furniture matching pipeline. First, Claude Vision looks at the render and identifies what's in it — sofa, coffee table, rug, whatever got placed in the scene. For each detected item it builds a search query, then hits Serper to run a live Google Shopping search. The results get filtered: we check they're actually furniture products, and we apply a budget filter — each item gets a per-item budget slice based on the user's total, with a 2x ceiling so nothing is wildly over. Top 5 results per item get rank-tier labels and are written to our `room_products` table. Each one becomes a shoppable hotspot on the render.

The affiliate layer then kicks in — product URLs get tagged for whichever network that retailer is on. Amazon Associates is the only active one right now, others like West Elm and Article are pending program approvals. A match failure never blocks the user from seeing their render — the room status just resets to complete regardless.
